newsitem.title: FRANCE: Japan car parts supplier to set up plant in France.
newsitem.headline: Japan car parts supplier to set up plant in France.

text.p: Japanese car parts supplier Ogura will set up its first European plant in the northern French town of Onnaing near the Belgian border, Ogura officials said on Wednesday.
Ogura estimates it will invest 177 million francs to set up the plant and employ 182 people by the year 2001, company officials told a news conference.
Ogura is a 60-year-old family-controlled specialist in the manufacture of clutches and air conditioning systems.
The Onnaing industrial zone benefits from EU subsidies -- a factor that influenced Ogura's decision, the officials said. Geographic location was also a factor.
"In the year 2001, we hope to produce 3.5 million parts, given that in a 200 km radius from the plant, two million cars are assembled yearly," said Akio Iwasaki, managing director of Ogura Europe.
Ogura has been established in the U.S. market for a decade and is now keen on establishing itself in Europe, where growth in car options outpaces car sales as a whole.

"In the United States, 80 percent of cars are equipped with air conditioning, 60 percent (have it) in Japan, and only 20 percent in France, but as young people want to listen to the radio with the windows rolled up, the air conditioning market will grow," Iwasaki said.

Ogura's decision to invest in the region, where General Motors' equipment supplier subsidiary Delphi Automotive Systems is present, underscores the importance of the industry in the area. Some 38,000 people are employed in the auto business in the region, representing 10 percent of the total in France.
